caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001274
attempts.paper_title: Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves for temporal interference stimulation
attempts.entry_title: Excitation and polarization of neurons by high-frequency sine waves (Semenov et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001274, which holds the strobe images of membrane polarization by pulses and sine waves (Figures 5, 6 and S3), and on the other dandisets of the same paper that hold the fast optical recordings of action potentials (001030, 001032, 001033, 001035, 001271, 001272). The strobe claims are blocked, as the dandisets hold no ROIs; the fast recordings test excitation by 2- and 20-kHz sine waves, thresholds, beat locking, the 2-s ramped stimulus and tetrodotoxin.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2025) from dandiset 001274 and the paper's other dandisets

outcomes.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 kHz and at 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, never as an on-off response.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
outcomes.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons. It was never an "on-off" response
outcomes.notes: At 2 kHz 27 of 28 neurons (96%) fired at least one AP under both AP readings, at 20 kHz 15 of 17 (88%), below the criterion's 90% at each frequency (measured gives the 20-kHz value). The bright-pixel trace gives the same, except 28 of 28 at 2 kHz under reading (b). The two neurons not excited at 20 kHz (001033/sub-7-2, 001035/sub-10-4) were tested up to 288 and 324 V/cm and fired in other sessions (26 and 11 APs). Their 20-kHz traces show no AP of 5%; sub-10-4 has 8 upticks of 2.5% at 324 V/cm on a falling trace (4 in all its pre-stimulus windows), which may be small APs that no reading counts; with it the fraction would be 16 of 17 (94%). Neither neuron is dimmer than the others (mean pre-stimulus images at the 78th and 74th percentiles of all recordings). The statement's "never as an on-off response" is not tested by the criterion. Neurons are pooled over 001032, 001033 and 001035.
deviations: The paper does not say which neurons or dandisets form Figure 1; all neurons tested with unmodulated 2- or 20-kHz sine waves in 001032, 001033 and 001035 are pooled.

F is the mean of the whole 16 x 16 frame (assumption; Methods, "The emission intensity over the entire cell soma (F)", but the files have no soma outline). It gives first APs of median 11.4% dF against the Methods' typical 11.3%. The brighter half of the frame is run as a variant and gives the same outcome.

AP peaks closer than 8 ms are merged, the AP duration of the Methods ("8 +- 0.7 ms duration"). Assumption: reading (a) also asks a prominence of 5% dF and a half-width of at least 1 ms (Methods: APs are "brief emission upticks" that "lasted about 10 ms"). Without them noise on a depolarized plateau counts as APs (about 18 per 250 ms on a synthetic 6% plateau with the data's noise, against 1.2 with them); 99% of the first APs of the data have a prominence above 8.6% and a half-width above 1.6 ms. The first version used a 2.5% prominence and no width. The first frame of every recording, a camera artifact, is left out of F0.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001032, 001033, 001034 and 001035 (assigned from their titles; the paper does not map figures to dandisets)

outcomes.statement: Near threshold, isolated APs appear 100 to 200 ms after the sine wave onset, and stronger fields shorten this delay and evoke sustained firing.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
outcomes.quote: at near-threshold electric field strengths, isolated APs emerged with a delay of 100-200 ms after the sine wave onset ... Increasing the field strength reduced this delay and evoked sustained firing
outcomes.notes: The median first-AP latency of the near-threshold sessions is 64 ms (reading a, IQR 37 to 128, n = 42 neuron-carrier pairs) and 67 ms (reading b), below 90 to 220 ms. By carrier it is 49 ms at 2 kHz (n = 27) and 124 ms (a) or 101 ms (b) at 20 kHz (n = 15). With only thresholds that have a lower-field session without APs it is 67 ms (n = 27). The second part holds; the latency falls with field (Spearman rho below 0) in 38 of 38 (a) and 39 of 39 (b) pairs with three or more fields with APs. The criterion needs both parts. 7 of 50 near-threshold sessions have a first AP within 20 ms; their traces show AP-shaped events, not stimulus artifacts (2.6 and 2.9 ms at 180 and 153 V/cm; of the other five, at 10 to 16 ms, three are the first of 4 regular APs, their lowest tested field being already above threshold, and two are single APs). The outcome depends on pooling 001032, 001033 and 001035, as the claims file's where does; the 001035 neurons alone give a median of 101 ms, inside 90 to 220 ms, and 001032 and 001033 give 50 and 58 ms.
deviations: Neuron-carrier pairs are the units for both parts (the criterion says per neuron and frequency); sessions repeated at one field are averaged, a standard choice.
Soma ROI and AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all.

outcomes.statement: The maximum firing rate increases linearly with field strength until it reaches a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1 inset
outcomes.quote: The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
outcomes.notes: The median ceiling over 29 neurons is 39.1 Hz under AP reading (a) (IQR 28.8 to 60.5, range 16.1 to 93.5) and 42.9 Hz under reading (b) (n = 31), both below 54 to 99 Hz; the bright-pixel trace gives 41.7 (a) and 61.7 Hz (b), the last the noisiest reading (1.18 false APs per 250 ms before stimuli). The rate rises with field before the ceiling in 32 of 32 neuron-carrier pairs (median slope 0.66 Hz per V/cm). The traces of the 35 sessions that set the ceilings are shown with the APs of both readings; 5 reach 79 to 94 Hz under both. The first version of reading (a) gave 59.9 Hz by counting plateau noise, at a rate near 80 Hz on synthetic traces; the revised reading (a) finds synthetic AP trains of 40 to 100 Hz at their rate. Three neurons never fired two APs in one unmodulated session and have no rate.
deviations: Assumption. Reading (a) asks a 5% prominence and a 1-ms half-width (as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all), so that noise on a depolarized plateau is not counted. The outcome rests on it under reading (a); reading (b), as the claims file gives it, yields the same outcome.
The detection cannot see rates above 125 Hz (8-ms merge, Methods' AP duration).

outcomes.statement: At the highest field strengths, APs coalesce into low-amplitude oscillations on a continuous depolarization, which can flatten and leave the membrane depolarized for the rest of the sine wave (an excitation block).
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
outcomes.quote: At the highest field strengths, multiple APs coalesced into low-amplitude oscillations on top of a continuous depolarization. These oscillations could flatten after several cycles, leaving the membrane depolarized for the rest of the sine wave
outcomes.notes: The highest-field unmodulated session has a last-100-ms mean dF above 5% and above the near-threshold session in 3 of 42 neuron-carrier pairs under both AP readings (3 of 42 and 3 of 43 with the bright-pixel trace), against more than half. The second-half variant also gives 3. The highest-field last-100-ms dF has a median of 1.3% (range -0.7 to 9.8). The highest field tested was a median 1.36 times the near-threshold field, and 11 of 370 unmodulated sessions have a last-100-ms dF above 5%, so most neurons may not have been driven far enough above threshold in the deposited sessions. The traces are not corrected for bleaching; the near-threshold sessions end at a median of -0.2%.
deviations: Soma ROI as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all. Sessions repeated at one field are averaged.

outcomes.statement: All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about twice those at 2 kHz, for modulated and unmodulated sine waves and for 1 and 5 APs.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)

statistics.n: n individual neurons per group (numbers in Figure 2D only)

outcomes.notes: Every 20-kHz threshold group is higher than the 2-kHz one with p below 0.0001 under both test readings (per group at most 2e-05, pooled 3e-24), but the ratios of mean thresholds (1 AP unmodulated, 1 AP modulated, 5 APs unmodulated, 5 APs modulated) are 2.27, 2.62, 2.37 and 2.82 under AP reading (a) and 2.29, 2.63, 2.28 and 2.82 under (b), all above 1.8 to 2.2; the criterion asks every ratio within it. The modulated 20-kHz groups have 2 or 3 neurons (all in 001033). The ratio does not depend on the field reading. The descriptions say the generator voltages overstate the amplitude by frequency-dependent factors not deposited. No such factor can rescue the claim; a 20-kHz factor relative to the 2-kHz one scales the four ratios alike, and they differ among themselves by a factor of 1.24, more than the 1.22 that the band 1.8 to 2.2 allows (the factor would need to be at least 0.794 and at most 0.779 under reading a, 0.791 and 0.779 under b).
deviations: Neurons of 001032, 001033 and 001035 pooled; the paper does not say which form Figure 2D.
The field per session is 36 V/cm times half the generator's peak-to-peak voltage, from the session descriptions, without frequency calibration (not in the dandisets).

outcomes.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves of the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency (for 2 kHz, 5 APs ... p = 0.0079; for 20 kHz, 1 and 5 APs, respectively ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037)
outcomes.notes: The modulated mean is higher in all three pairs under both readings. Under reading (a) two pairs reach p < 0.05 (20 kHz 1 AP p = 0.021, 20 kHz 5 APs p = 0.017; 2 kHz 5 APs p = 0.069); under reading (b) the same two (p = 0.021 and 0.012; 2 kHz 5 APs p = 0.155). The 20-kHz modulated groups have 3 neurons for 1 AP and 2 for 5 APs. The 2-kHz 1-AP pair, for which the paper reports no difference, gives unpaired p = 0.059 (a) and 0.045 (b), and paired p below 0.001 on 12 neurons. Paired tests on the three pairs give p from 0.12 to 0.29.
deviations: As in fig2d-20khz-twofold-threshold.

outcomes.statement: The AP threshold for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves was 57.7 plus or minus 3.6 V/cm.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 6; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: the AP threshold of 57.7 ± 3.6 V/cm for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves ( Figure 2D )
outcomes.notes: The mean 1-AP threshold for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves is 75.6 +- 6.2 V/cm (n = 27, reading a) and 74.8 +- 5.9 (reading b) with the field as 36 V/cm times half the peak-to-peak voltage, and 151.2 and 149.6 V/cm with the whole of it; none is within 57.7 +- 3.6. By dandiset it is 92.2 (001032, n = 10), 76.6 (001033, n = 7) and 58.3 V/cm (001035, n = 10). With only thresholds bracketed by a lower-field session without APs, 88.0 V/cm (n = 16). The half reading fits the paper's numbers: 63 and 81 V/cm are 3.5 and 4.5 Vpp under it (2 and 7 sessions) and 1.75 and 2.25 Vpp under the full reading (no session). The generator voltage overstates the amplitude by a frequency-dependent factor that is not deposited; a 2-kHz factor of 0.76 would give 57.7 V/cm, and the only measured factors in the paper's dandisets (2-us pulses, 001273, another electrode array) are 0.62 to 0.79. The miss may come from the calibration. The outcome also depends on pooling the three dandisets, as the claims file's where does; 001035 alone gives 58.3 V/cm, inside 57.7 +- 3.6. 001035 has no modulated sessions, so Figure 2D cannot come from it alone, and which neurons the paper used cannot be settled.
deviations: The field conversion is the dandisets' (36 V/cm per volt) with two readings of the voltage; both give the same outcome. No frequency calibration is applied, as the factors are not in the dandisets.

outcomes.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold is locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves trigger no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Firing locks to the beats; of the APs in the 22 modulated sessions with 5 APs or more, 0.96 (a) and 0.98 (b) fall 12.5 to 37.5 ms into a beat, against 0.04 of the APs pooled over all modulated sessions with the beats shifted by 25 ms, so (ii) holds. (i) holds under both readings (at most 8 and 6 APs). (iii) fails under both: one session (001032/sub-2-1, 198 V/cm) ends with a last-100-ms dF of 5.9%, above its near-threshold modulated session (-0.2% at 144 V/cm), so it meets the block test. The criterion asks all three parts.
deviations: The beats are counted from the stimulus onset at 50 ms, with the envelope at zero there (the claims file's reading of the beat); the data support it, as the shifted beats show.
Part (ii) is read on the APs pooled over the sessions with 5 APs or more; per session, 21 of 22 sessions have 80% or more in the window under both readings.

outcomes.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves trigger more APs than modulated ones.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
outcomes.quote: At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
outcomes.notes: In 52 pairs from 12 neurons (same neuron, carrier and generator voltage), the unmodulated sine wave gave more APs in 47, fewer in none and as many in 5, a mean of 3.70 more (reading a, paired t p = 7.3e-10); reading (b) 46 and 1, p = 2.5e-09; the bright-pixel trace 47 or 44 and 0 or 2. By carrier, 39 of 44 pairs at 2 kHz and 8 of 8 at 20 kHz (reading a).
deviations: Counts repeated at one field are averaged per pair, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Replacing NaCl with sodium gluconate, lowering conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm, reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
outcomes.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
outcomes.notes: No session of 001032, 001033 or 001035 is described as recorded in the sodium gluconate solution; every description gives the standard NaCl solution. 001030 is in sodium gluconate but holds only 2-s ramped stimuli. The NaCl and NaGlu sessions of Figures 3A and 3B, if deposited, cannot be told apart. Nor do the thresholds show a hidden switch: of 47 neuron-carrier pairs with two or more ascending voltage series with APs, none has a series whose threshold drops to 0.6 or less of the series before and after it.

outcomes.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped up over 250 ms evoked sustained firing for the whole stimulus; firing rate rose with field strength until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization, which developed before the end of the ramp.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization. The block had already developed before the end of the 250-ms ramp-up period
outcomes.notes: Tested on neuron c7 of 001030, the only neuron with a trace without APs (1.0 V), which the Methods' bleaching correction needs. (i) APs occur in the last 250 ms at 52, 61 and 72 V/cm (8 to 10 under both readings). (ii) The AP count rises with field, from 0 at 36 V/cm to 89 (a) or 90 (b) at 61 V/cm, then 88 and 13 (a) or 80 and 8 (b). (iii) At the highest field, 83 V/cm, the mean dF over 0.25 to 2 s is 6.7% and the APs stop within the ramp; reading (a) finds 5 peaks after 250 ms (0.34 to 1.74 s) and reading (b) one (1.68 s). Measured on this trace (notebook section 11), noise alone gives as many detections over 0.25 to 2 s as were found (residual SD 0.94%, against 0.89% before the stimulus; mirrored trace 6 (a) and 7 (b); running median plus Gaussian noise a mean of 7.8 (a) and 5.1 (b), 5 or more in 91% of draws under (a), 1 or more in 99% under (b); shuffled residual 8.4 and 4.6), and about 1.1 (a) and 0.7 (b) per 250-ms window against the 8 to 10 APs of part (i). Read as no more detections after 250 ms than the trace's noise gives, (iii) holds. Taken literally, no APs after 250 ms, it fails under both readings, as it would on any plateau above 5% with this noise; the outcome was not_reproduced until the third verification round. The test rests on c7 alone. The other three neurons, corrected with the same trace, reach no block, which the criterion does not count against the claim.
deviations: Assumption. Part (iii) is read as no more detections after 250 ms than the noise of the bleaching-corrected trace gives, measured on the trace itself, as the claims file's AP readings have no allowance for false detections on a depolarized plateau and the Methods give no detection rule. The outcome rests on it.
The field is 36 V/cm times the one-polarity voltage that 001030 gives.
The other neurons are corrected with c7's AP-free trace, as they have none of their own.
Two recordings of neuron c5 have 6,000 frames, which end before the 2-s stimulus does.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS instead of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, stimulation near threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs and stronger fields induced sustained firing ending in sustained depolarization, as with FluoVolt.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs. Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: 001272 holds 3 neurons, where the paper used eight. The readings disagree on excitation (3 of 3 neurons under reading a at 5% and under both 5-SD readings, 1 of 3 under reading b at 5%), but under every reading no neuron meets the block test at its highest field (0 of 3; inverted last-100-ms dF 0.7%, 3.3% and 1.6%), so the claim fails under all of them for the neurons deposited and the disagreement does not decide the outcome. Latency falls with field in 1 of 2 neurons with three fields with APs under reading (a), and 2 of 3 under the 5-SD readings. Whether the five neurons not deposited would change this cannot be known.
deviations: Only 3 of the paper's 8 neurons are in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization caused by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2
outcomes.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: In all 6 neurons recorded in tetrodotoxin (3.6 to 11 min after the normal-solution session at the same field), APs present before are absent under reading (a); under reading (b) 5 of 6, as (b) finds 5% rises in 15 of 17 tetrodotoxin sessions of one neuron. The last-100-ms dF in tetrodotoxin is at most 0.4% in every session. Only 1 of the 6 neurons had a last-100-ms dF above 5% before tetrodotoxin (5.4%, falling to -0.7%), and no session of the 14 neurons never put in tetrodotoxin did (0 of 171), so the criterion, which asks the depolarization block of every tetrodotoxin neuron, fails in 5 of 6. The vehicle neuron of Figure S2 is not identified in the files; the neurons never put in tetrodotoxin stand in for it.
deviations: The compared field is the highest recorded both before and in tetrodotoxin, with the latest normal session and the first tetrodotoxin session at it; the paper says "about 5 min after".
No neuron is labelled as the vehicle control of Figure S2; all normal-solution sessions carry the same "vehicle control" text.

outcomes.statement: Elongated neurons aligned with the field have about twice the charging and discharging time constants of the same cells perpendicular to it, or of randomly shaped cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4A, 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants, as compared to either the same cells oriented perpendicular to the field ( p < 0.001, paired t test) or to randomly shaped cells ( p < 0.01, unpaired t test)

statistics.about: elongated parallel cells against random cells

outcomes.notes: 001273 holds raw strobe stacks only (181 files, 13 subjects). The ROIs over the most de- and hyperpolarized regions are not deposited (claims file O1), no file says which cell is elongated or random, and the field direction is in the descriptions of 118 of 181 files only (up-bottom or right-left). The parallel, perpendicular and random groups cannot be formed.

outcomes.statement: The maximum optical TMP and the charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles, indicating no rectification of the field.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field. Charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the two poles either
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-orientation-time-constants; the paper's ROIs are not in 001273, and the 19 experiments cannot be matched to its 13 subjects.

outcomes.statement: Discharging time constants were larger than charging ones in the same cell, except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test), with the exception of elongated cells aligned with the field
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-orientation-time-constants (no ROIs, no shape groups in 001273).

outcomes.statement: Pooled over all 19 experiments, the charging and discharging time constants were 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes exceed 95% of full charge within 3 us.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E (ALL)
outcomes.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4-orientation-time-constants; no ROIs in 001273, and its 13 subjects cannot be matched to the 19 experiments.

outcomes.statement: During a single beat of a 2-kHz sine wave, the optical TMP in ROIs 1 and 2 oscillates with the carrier in opposite phases, with amplitude proportional to the sine wave amplitude, on top of a gradual whole-cell depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 2; Figures 5C, 5D and 5H
outcomes.quote: Optical TMP oscillated in synchrony with the carrier sine wave in the opposite phases ... These oscillations, proportional to the sine wave amplitude, were superimposed on the gradual depolarization of the entire cell
outcomes.notes: 001274 holds raw strobe stacks only; the ROIs 1 and 2 are not deposited (claims file O1), and cell C7 cannot be identified (O4). No subject has 12 sessions at 100 Hz (at most 5), as the cell of Figure 5 had. With ROIs rebuilt from the RATIO image (a variant only, section 14), ROI 2 oscillates in antiphase to ROI 1 in 7 of 9 candidate subjects.

outcomes.statement: During the sine wave beat the whole cell gradually depolarizes as the sine wave amplitude grows, then repolarizes.
outcomes.source: Figure 5C and 5D legend; Figures 5C and 5D
outcomes.quote: These high-frequency oscillations superimpose a gradual whole-cell depolarization that develops as the sine wave amplitude increases
outcomes.notes: As fig5-carrier-antiphasic; cell C7 and its ROIs cannot be identified in 001274.

outcomes.statement: In the cell of Figure 5, the 2-us pulse depolarized ROI 2 about 30% less than it hyperpolarized ROI 1, while the sine wave oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than in ROI 1.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figures 5B to 5D
outcomes.quote: Unexpectedly, in this cell, the oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than those in ROI 1 (compared to just 30% smaller when the same cell was polarized with the 2-μs pulse)
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig6c-sine-sensitivity; cell C7 and its ROIs cannot be identified in 001274.

outcomes.statement: In a second neuron (Figure S3), polarization in ROI 1 was 20% smaller than in ROI 2 with the 2-us pulse and 40% smaller with sine waves, and the antiphasic oscillations did not move to a new area.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 3; Figure S3
outcomes.quote: With the 2-μs pulse, polarization in ROI 1 was 20% smaller than in ROI 2 ( Figure S3B ); however, with sine waves, it became 40% smaller
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig5-sine-asymmetry-c7; cell C8 and its ROIs cannot be identified in 001274.

outcomes.statement: Over 16 further ROIs around the cell of Figure 5, strong oscillations were found on one side only, and the relatively large oscillations of ROIs 12 to 14 on the other side were not antiphasic to them, so the small ROI 2 oscillations did not come from migration of the polarized area.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 2; Figures 5E to 5G
outcomes.quote: strong oscillations were observed on one side only ( Figure 5F ), and the relatively large oscillations in ROIs 12-14 in Figure 5G were not antiphasic to those in Figure 5F
outcomes.notes: The 16 further ROIs of Figure 5E and their split between Figures 5F and 5G are not in 001274, and cell C7 cannot be identified.

outcomes.statement: The FluoVolt response to 2-us pulses, averaged 1 to 2 us into the pulse, ranged from 15% to 47% per 1 kV/cm, averaging 28% plus or minus 2.5% over all ROIs in the nine cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 4; Figure 6B
outcomes.quote: The electric field sensitivity of FluoVolt ranged between a 15% and 47% change per 1 kV/cm, with an average value of 28% ± 2.5% across all ROIs in all the cells
outcomes.notes: No ROIs in 001274 (claims file O1), no field in V/cm, and no identifier for cells C1 to C9. Nine subjects have a pulse and 100-Hz sessions, consistent with C1 to C9 but not shown to be them. As a variant only, ROIs rebuilt from the Methods' RATIO image (8 x 8 pixel squares at its extremes in the cell) with the paper's 257 V/cm for a 10-V pulse, scaled by the voltage, give 19.5 +- 2.4 %/kV/cm over 18 ROIs, range 4.3 to 43.9 (paper 28 +- 2.5, 15 to 47). The frame times are an assumption (50-ns steps from 1 us before the pulse, all nine pulses described as forward); the ROI difference is above half its maximum from frame 25 to 62, against frames 20 to 59 for the pulse. The rebuilt ROIs are placed on the image they are measured on, which biases the value upwards.

outcomes.statement: The sine-wave-induced TMP oscillations were linearly correlated with the electric field (p below 0.01% for both ROIs in eight of the nine cells), with sensitivities from 1.5% to 28.4% per 1 kV/cm.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 5; Figure 6C
outcomes.quote: The oscillations displayed a robust linear correlation with the electric field ... <0.01% for both ROIs in eight cells. The regression coefficient, which was the FluoVolt sensitivity to sine waves, varied from 1.5% to 28.4%

statistics.test: linear regression of emission change on electric field strength
statistics.n: both ROIs in eight of the nine cells

outcomes.notes: No ROIs, no waveform and no field in 001274. As a variant only, the rebuilt ROIs on the 100-Hz sessions of the nine candidate subjects, regressed frame by frame on a signed field built from the paper's 136 V/cm peak and a carrier phase fitted to ROI 1, give 5.5 +- 0.8 %/kV/cm (span 0.75; range 0.2 to 12.9), with p below 0.0001 in 8 of 18 ROIs, and the same at spans 0.5 and 0.25. Fitting the phase on ROI 1 forces its slope positive and inflates its p-value.

outcomes.statement: Every ROI's sensitivity to sine waves was smaller than to the pulse; averaged over all ROIs it was 11.8% plus or minus 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, 42% of the pulse value.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 5; Figures 6C and 6D
outcomes.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig6b-pulse-sensitivity and fig6c-sine-sensitivity. In the variant with rebuilt ROIs the sine value is below the pulse value in 17 of 18 ROIs, and the mean sine value is 28% of the mean pulse value (paper 42%).

outcomes.statement: Combining the sine wave sensitivity (11.8% per kV/cm) with the 2-kHz AP threshold (57.7 V/cm) gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV at FluoVolt's calibration of about 10% per 100 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig6d-sine-less-than-pulse, blocked. Its other input, the 2-kHz threshold, is not reproduced here (75.6 V/cm against 57.7).
outcomes.where: DANDI:001032, 001033, 001034 and 001035 for the threshold (assigned from their titles); the sensitivity from this dataset

findings.statement: DANDI:001274 holds only raw strobe image stacks (512 x 512 pixels). It has no ROIs, no RATIO images, no frame times, no electric field in V/cm (only generator volts) and no identifier linking its 20 subjects to the paper's cells C1 to C9, C7 (Figure 5) and C8 (Figure S3). The claims of Figures 5, 6 and S3 cannot be tested as the paper made them.

DANDI:001273 (Figure 4) holds only raw strobe stacks. The ROIs, each cell's shape group (elongated or random) and, in 63 of 181 files, the field direction are not given, so the paper's 19 experiments and groups cannot be formed from its 13 subjects.

DANDI:001034 is a second deposit of DANDI:001032. The subjects match (sub-N-3 against sub-N-1), all 178 assets match one to one by session start time and size (116 also by name), and the image arrays and start times of ten compared pairs are identical. Each recording is counted once here.

The session descriptions of tetrodotoxin recordings in DANDI:001271 and DANDI:001274 say that tetrodotoxin "abolished the action potentials and caused sustained depolarization". The paper says it "fully blocked the sustained depolarization", and in 001271 the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus is at most 0.4% in every tetrodotoxin session.
No 250-ms session in DANDI:001032, 001033 or 001035 is described as recorded in the sodium gluconate solution of Figures 3A and 3B; all give the NaCl solution.

The fast recordings give the generator's peak-to-peak voltage and "1V translates into 36 V/cm", but say the voltage is not the measured amplitude and that frequency-dependent calibration factors "will be reported separately"; they are not in the dandisets. DANDI:001030 gives one-polarity volts. Whether the 36 V/cm applies to the peak-to-peak or the peak voltage is not stated.
DANDI:001272 holds 3 neurons recorded with Di-8-ANEPPS; the paper reports eight.

The fast recordings are 16 x 16 pixels, where the paper's Methods give 64 x 64 after binning, and 59 of 178 sessions of 001032 have 900 frames, one has 1,400 and one 1,800, against 1,200 in the Methods. The first frame of every fast recording is a bright artifact (median 3.05 times the other pre-stimulus frames).
The descriptions of DANDI:001032 to 001035 give a 140-um gap between the stimulating electrodes; the paper's Methods and DANDI:001274 give 120 um.
DANDI:001030 makes one subject per session (sub-c7-1-45V and so on), so its 17 subjects are 4 neurons (c5 to c8). Two of its recordings (c5) have 6,000 frames and end before the 2-s stimulus does.
Many strobe sessions of DANDI:001274 recorded on 2024-08-24 are described as made in 1 uM tetrodotoxin, which the paper does not mention for Figures 5, 6 or S3.

Question for the paper's authors. Which pixels form the soma ROI (F) of the fast recordings, given the deposited 16 x 16 frames? This attempt assumed the whole frame, whose APs have the Methods' typical size (median 11.4% dF against 11.3%), and ran the brighter half as a variant; the outcomes do not change between them.

Question for the paper's authors. How were the generator voltages of the fast recordings converted to the field in V/cm (peak or peak-to-peak, and with which frequency calibration)? This attempt assumed 36 V/cm times half the peak-to-peak voltage, which matches the voltages behind the paper's 63 and 81 V/cm; the 2-kHz threshold is 75.6 V/cm with it and 151 V/cm with the whole voltage, against the paper's 57.7, which a 2-kHz calibration factor of 0.76 would give.

Question for the paper's authors. What rule counted APs, for example two APs close together, APs riding on a depolarization, or small upticks below 5% dF? This attempt assumed a peak above 5% dF over F0 that also rises 5% above the trace around it and is at least 1 ms wide at half its height; without the last two conditions, noise on a depolarized plateau counts as APs and the maximum firing rate ceiling moves from 39.1 to 59.9 Hz.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive metadata and tested the AP detection on synthetic traces. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; agrees compares that outcome with the record as it stood before this revision. It found three problems that affect a conclusion: reading (a) counted noise on a depolarized plateau as APs, the generator calibration was not estimated, and the summary scored as partial claims whose criteria have no partial outcome.

disagreements.reason: 2 kHz passes (27/28 or 28/28), but 20 kHz is 15/17 = 88% under all four readings. The criterion needs at least 90% at each frequency and has no partial outcome. The two neurons that never fired were tested up to 288 and 324 V/cm, above the mean 20-kHz threshold of 171 V/cm.

Latency falls with field in 38/38 pairs, but the median near-threshold latency is 54 to 67 ms under every reading. The variant that keeps only bracketed thresholds gives 67 ms. Both are outside 90 to 220 ms, and the criterion needs both parts.

On the adopted whole-frame trace the two AP readings disagree: 59.9 Hz under (a) is inside 54 to 99 Hz, 42.9 Hz under (b) is outside. The fig1 criterion that this claim inherits blocks when readings disagree. The notebook's reproduced ignores reading (b).

p < 0.0001 holds pooled and nearly always per group. The 20/2 kHz ratios are 2.27 to 2.82, outside 1.8 to 2.2, except two groups under bright/b. The criterion needs every ratio within tolerance. The outcome also depends on frequency-dependent generator calibration.

(ii) passes: 0.83 to 0.98 of APs fall in the peak window. (iii) fails under every reading: one session has 5.9% in the last 100 ms. (i) fails under whole/a, bright/a and bright/b, with up to 13 APs in a session.

(i) and (ii) pass for c7. (iii) fails under both readings at 82.8 V/cm: reading (a) finds 131 APs after 250 ms, reading (b) finds one (at 1.682 s); rest dF is 6.7%. Reading (a)'s count is probably noise on the plateau, and reading (b) misses by one AP.
APs are abolished in 6/6 neurons under (a) and 5/6 under (b). Only 1 of 6 neurons has last-100-ms dF above 5% before TTX, so the depolarization part fails. The vehicle neuron was not identified.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the attempt record, the README, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. It agreed with 25 of 26 outcomes and now disagrees with fig3c-sustained-firing-2s; it quoted seven sentences the numbers do not support (the fig2d calibration estimate, the short-latency APs, brightness, the shifted-beat fraction, a round-1 count, the RATIO image in the README, the frame counts) and asked that the outcomes of fig1-onset-delay and threshold-2khz-unmodulated be said to depend on pooling the dandisets.

disagreements.reason: Parts (i) and (ii) hold for c7. Part (iii) fails only on 5 events under (a) and 1 under (b) on the 6.7% plateau over 0.25 to 2 s. The notebook's own test gives 1.2 (a) and 0.8 (b) false APs per 250 ms on a 6% plateau at 0.83% noise, which predicts about 8 and 6 such events over 1.75 s, and more on a bleaching-corrected (differenced, so noisier) trace. The events are isolated and irregular. It would score c7 reproduced; at the least the outcome should be marked assumed, since it rests on treating noise-level detections as APs.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 3. The one proposed change of outcome, fig3c-sustained-firing-2s to reproduced, and the analysis behind it in notebook cells 57 and 59 (the false-detection rate measured on c7's bleaching-corrected trace), with the attempt record and the claims file. Nothing else was reviewed.

entries.name: 001048-semenov-2025
entries.title: High-frequency sine waves excite isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025). Dandiset 001048 names the paper but holds HEK-cell recordings of another study, so the claims are tested on the ten dandisets the paper lists (001030 to 001035, 001271 to 001274). These hold optical recordings of rat hippocampal neurons stimulated by unmodulated and 20-Hz modulated sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz, with TTX and Di-8-ANEPPS controls, and strobe images of membrane charging by 2-us pulses and sine waves.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2025) from the DANDI datasets it names

entries.name: 001274-semenov-2025
entries.title: Excitation and polarization of neurons by high-frequency sine waves (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001274, which holds the strobe images of membrane polarization by pulses and sine waves (Figures 5, 6 and S3), and on the other dandisets of the same paper that hold the fast optical recordings of action potentials (001030, 001032, 001033, 001035, 001271, 001272). The strobe claims are blocked, as the dandisets hold no ROIs; the fast recordings test excitation by 2- and 20-kHz sine waves, thresholds, beat locking, the 2-s ramped stimulus and tetrodotoxin.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2025) from dandiset 001274 and the paper's other dandisets
